headline: Meesho Limited: SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) Disclosure by Sanjeev Kumar
sum: Sanjeev Kumar has filed a disclosure under SEBI Regulation 31(4), the Takeover Code provision requiring disclosure of substantial acquisition of shares in listed companies. The filing was submitted to NSE on or around 22–24 June 2026.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure signals a cross-threshold shareholding event (typically ≥5% or a further material tranche); counsel must verify the exact threshold breached, any standstill undertakings, and whether open-offer triggers apply under Regulation 26 of the SAST Code.
detail: The disclosure was made under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, a regulatory framework governing large shareholding acquisitions in listed Indian companies. Regulation 31(4) mandates disclosure to the stock exchange (here NSE) when a person or group acquires or proposes to acquire shares crossing material thresholds. The filing by Sanjeev Kumar indicates a material change in shareholding structure at Meesho Limited. No public announcement details regarding the value, number of shares, acquisition price, or conditions have been disclosed in accessible sources.

Central to this filing; mandates disclosure to stock exchange of substantial acquisition crossing specified thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 50%, 75%); triggers ongoing disclosure obligations.
Open-offer trigger; if acquisition crosses specified thresholds (typically 25%), an open offer may be mandated unless exemptions apply.
Defines 'person', 'group', and 'associate' for attribution of shareholding; critical for determining if disclosing party acts alone or as part of a concert.
Overarching statute under which SEBI is constituted and takeover rules are issued; establishes regulatory framework for stock exchange listed companies.
Shareholding disclosure, director appointment, board composition, and general corporate governance; may intersect if disclosing party becomes director or seeks board seat.
